title: Best Time for Sandakphu: Views, Flowers and Snow
meta_description: When to trek Sandakphu: clear Everest views Oct–Dec, rhododendrons Apr–May, snow Jan–Feb, and the monsoon park closure mid-June to mid-September.
summary: Go in October to early December for the clearest views of Everest and Kanchenjunga, and in April and May for rhododendrons in flower with hazier skies. January and February bring snow and the cleanest air but hard cold. The park usually closes for the monsoon from mid-June to mid-September.

sections.heading: The short answer
paras: Sandakphu has two good seasons and they reward different people. Autumn, from late September to early December, is the season for mountains: the monsoon has washed the haze out of the air, and on most mornings the whole line from Everest to Kanchenjunga stands clear. Spring, from late March to May, is the season for forests: the rhododendrons, magnolias and primulas flower along the ridge, but by mid-morning the views often disappear into haze and cloud.

If you can choose only one, and the Everest view matters most, go in the last two weeks of October or in November. If you want colour, birdsong and warmer nights, go in mid to late April. Avoid the monsoon months altogether. Singalila National Park usually closes from about mid-June to mid-September, and even outside the closure, June and September mean leeches, landslides on the jeep roads and days of cloud. Closure dates are fixed each year by the park, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Month by month on the ridge
paras: These are the conditions we plan around at Sandakphu itself, at 3,636 m. Maneybhanjan, at about 2,150 m, is 8–10 °C warmer, and the Srikhola and Rimbik end of the trek warmer still. Night temperatures in lodges with no heating are close to outside temperatures by morning.

sections.heading: Autumn: the season for mountains
paras: The first clear mornings usually come in early October, once the monsoon has pulled back. From then until mid-December, Sandakphu shows what it is famous for: the Kanchenjunga massif filling the north as the Sleeping Buddha, and to the west the summits of Everest, Lhotse and Makalu, with the Three Sisters and Chamlang between them. Four of the five highest peaks on earth from one cold hilltop.

October is also the busiest month. Durga Puja and the school holidays fill lodges at Tumling and Sandakphu, Land Rovers run full, and the best rooms go weeks ahead. November is our favourite: the skies are often even cleaner, the crowds thin out after Diwali, and the grass on the ridge turns gold. Nights drop below freezing, so carry a proper down jacket.

December keeps the views and adds the chance of the first snow. Days are short, with sunrise around 6 am and dark by 5 pm, so start walking early. Over Christmas and New Year, lodges fill again with trekkers from Kolkata.

sections.heading: Spring: the season for rhododendrons
paras: Singalila is one of the best rhododendron walks in the eastern Himalaya, and the flowering climbs the ridge with the season. The red tree rhododendron, Rhododendron arboreum, opens first in the forests above Chitrey and Meghma from March. In April the pink and white magnolias and the bigger-leaved species flower around Tonglu, Gairibas and Kalipokhri. By late April and May the bloom has reached the upper ridge near Sandakphu and toward Phalut, where the hardier species flower among the fir.

Exact timing moves by two or three weeks from year to year with the winter's snow and the spring's warmth. Mid-April is the safest bet for colour across most of the trail. The trade-off is the sky: spring haze from the plains and forest fires can hide the big peaks by 8 or 9 am, and afternoon thunderstorms are common in May. Get up before dawn and you still have a good chance of Kanchenjunga, but Everest, much further away, shows less often.

sections.heading: Winter: snow and cold
paras: From late December to February, snow can fall anywhere above Tonglu, and Sandakphu may sit under it for weeks. The air is at its clearest, the trail at its quietest, and a snowy Sandakphu morning is a sight few trekkers see. It is also hard going. Nights fall well below freezing, lodges have only a wood or yak-dung stove in the dining room, water pipes freeze, and the Land Rover track can be closed by ice or deep snow for days.

Go in winter only with proper gear: a four-season sleeping bag or a liner plus the lodge's heavy quilts, a down jacket, gloves, microspikes for icy stretches and waterproof boots. Some lodges at the upper stops close for part of the winter. Ask at Maneybhanjan before setting out, since snow and track closures change week by week; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Monsoon and the closure
paras: Singalila National Park usually closes from mid-June to mid-September. The reason is partly safety, with landslides on the jeep roads and swollen streams on the descent, and partly the wildlife, since it is breeding season in the forest. Even before the closure, June brings heavy rain, leeches below about 2,800 m and days without a single view.

Late September, once the park reopens, can be a fine time for a quiet trek with green forests, but expect some rain and cloud until the monsoon fully withdraws, usually in early October. The exact closing and opening dates are notified by the park each year; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Which season suits which traveller
paras: We match the month to the person more than to the calendar. A few rules of thumb from years of sending friends up the ridge:
list: First-time trekkers and families with children: late October or November, when the trail is dry, the days are settled and the reward at the top is almost certain.
Photographers chasing the Sleeping Buddha and Everest in one frame: November and early December, when the air is cleanest and the light low and warm at dawn and dusk.
Birders and people who love forests: April and early May, when rhododendrons flower, birds are singing and nesting, and red pandas are sometimes active in the bamboo.
Experienced winter walkers: January and February, for snow and empty lodges, with full cold-weather gear and a flexible plan if the track closes.
Budget travellers: early November or late March, outside the Puja and Christmas peaks, when lodges are easier to find and rooms are sometimes cheaper.
Anyone with only a long weekend: a Land Rover round trip in November gives the best odds of a clear view for the time spent.

sections.heading: Timing tips we follow
paras: A few habits make more difference than the month you pick.
list: Build in a spare day at Sandakphu or Kalipokhri, so one cloudy morning does not cost you the view you came for.
Be outside 20 minutes before sunrise; the first light on Kanchenjunga lasts only a few minutes.
In spring, walk early and expect cloud from late morning; in autumn, the evenings are often clear too.
Avoid Durga Puja week and the Christmas to New Year stretch if you want a room without booking far ahead.
Check the Darjeeling forecast the night before a Land Rover trip; vehicles cost the same whether or not the peaks show.

faqs.q: What is the best month to visit Sandakphu?
faqs.a: November, for the clearest and most reliable views of Everest and Kanchenjunga with fewer crowds than October. Late October and early December are almost as good. If you want rhododendrons in flower instead, go in mid to late April, accepting hazier skies. Avoid June to mid-September, when the park is usually closed for the monsoon.

faqs.q: When do rhododendrons bloom on the Sandakphu trek?
faqs.a: From March to May, climbing the ridge with the season. Red tree rhododendrons flower first in the lower forests above Chitrey in March, the middle stretch around Tonglu and Gairibas peaks in April, and the upper ridge near Sandakphu and Phalut in late April and May. Timing shifts by two to three weeks from year to year.

faqs.q: Can I see Everest from Sandakphu in April?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but less reliably than in autumn. Spring haze and cloud usually build by mid-morning, so your best chance is at sunrise. Kanchenjunga, about 70 km away, shows more often than Everest, which is about 140 km away. For a near-certain Everest view, go between mid-October and early December.

Yes. Snow can fall from December to March, most often in January and February, and occasionally in late autumn or spring storms. Sandakphu can stay snowbound for weeks and the Land Rover track may close. Nights fall to about −8 °C or lower. If you want snow, go in January or February with proper winter gear and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Singalila National Park closed in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Usually yes, from about mid-June to mid-September, for safety and the wildlife breeding season. The exact dates are notified by the park each year, and some local trekking and Land Rover trips may operate on non-park stretches. Check current status before you travel, and avoid planning a trek for late June or early September.

faqs.q: How cold is Sandakphu in October?
faqs.a: Daytime temperatures are usually 8–12 °C in sun and nights drop to about 0–2 °C, colder with wind. By late October and November nights fall below freezing. Lodges are unheated except for the dining room stove, so bring a down jacket, a warm hat, gloves and thermal layers, and use the lodge quilts.

faqs.q: Is December a good time for the Sandakphu trek?
faqs.a: Yes, if you can handle the cold. December skies are usually very clear, crowds are lower than in October, and there is a chance of the first snow. Nights fall to about −5 °C, days are short and some tracks can ice up. Bring proper winter layers and expect higher demand over Christmas and New Year.

In Durga Puja week and on October weekends, yes. Lodges at Tumling and Sandakphu fill, the best rooms go weeks in advance and Land Rovers run full. Weekdays in early November are much quieter with equally clear skies. If October is your only option, book lodges through your guide well ahead.

faqs.q: Can I trek Sandakphu in September?
faqs.a: Only in the second half, after the park reopens, usually around mid-September. Expect some rain, cloud and leeches on the lower forest stretches until the monsoon withdraws in early October. The forests are green and the trail is quiet. Check current status of the park reopening date and the jeep roads before you travel.
